speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you are experiencing knee pain after recently increasing your physical activity. To help me determine the exact cause, can you tell me precisely where the pain is located on your knee and whether it started during a specific movement?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the history of repetitive pivoting and twisting in volleyball, is the pain localized specifically to the inner (medial) side of your knee? Additionally, do you feel any instability or "giving way" of the knee during movement?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial tibial stress syndrome (shin splints). The location of your pain directly over the medial tibia, combined with recent increased physical activity in a high-impact sport like volleyball, is highly characteristic of this condition. Have you noticed any swelling or tenderness when pressing along the inner edge of your shin bone?
